subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If the tangent at any point on the curve x²⁄³ + y²⁄³ = a²⁄³ intersects the coordinate axes in A and B, show that the length AB is a constant.

mark_split.label: Take a general point in parametric form
Find the slope of the tangent
Write the tangent and read off A and B
Find AB and show it is free of θ

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what point you take on the curve, how you get the two intercepts, and what has to happen to θ at the end.

steps.label: Take a general point in parametric form
steps.margin_note: First mark. The question says at ANY point, so the point must be general. The parametric form removes the two-thirds powers before any differentiation starts, which is why it is written first even though the question never mentions θ.
lines: The curve is x²⁄³ + y²⁄³ = a²⁄³.
Take the general point P = (a cos³θ, a sin³θ) on the curve.
Check that P lies on it:
(a cos³θ)²⁄³ + (a sin³θ)²⁄³ = a²⁄³cos²θ + a²⁄³sin²θ
= a²⁄³(cos²θ + sin²θ) = a²⁄³
So P is a point of the curve for every value of θ.

recall.must_convey: That a general point is taken as (a cos³θ, a sin³θ) and it satisfies the curve.
accept: take the parametric point a cos cubed theta comma a sin cubed theta
use the parametric form so the two thirds powers disappear
take a general point on the curve with a parameter theta
parametric point teesukoni curve meeda undi ani chupinchali
put x equal to a cos cubed theta and y equal to a sin cubed theta
verify the point satisfies the equation of the curve

steps.why: Raising a cos³θ to the power 2/3 leaves cos²θ, so the awkward index disappears in one line. Working with x and y directly needs implicit differentiation with x⁻¹⁄³ terms, which is longer and harder to keep clean.
common_mistakes: Taking a numbered point with fixed values, which proves nothing about ANY point.
Writing the point as (a cos²θ, a sin²θ), which does not satisfy the curve.
Skipping the check that P lies on the curve.
steps.memory_tip: The power on the curve is 2/3, so the power inside the point is 3 — the cube inside cancels the two-thirds outside.

steps.label: Find the slope of the tangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Differentiate x and y separately with respect to θ, then divide. The factor 3a cancels, so the slope depends only on θ.
lines: x = a cos³θ  ⇒  dx/dθ = 3a cos²θ · (−sinθ) = −3a cos²θ sinθ
y = a sin³θ  ⇒  dy/dθ = 3a sin²θ · cosθ
dy/dx = (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ) = (3a sin²θ cosθ)/(−3a cos²θ sinθ)
= −sinθ/cosθ
∴ slope of the tangent  m = −tanθ

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx is dy/dθ divided by dx/dθ and comes to −tanθ.
accept: differentiate x and y with respect to theta and divide
dy by dx equals dy by d theta over dx by d theta
the slope is minus tan theta
theta tho differentiate chesi divide cheyyali
three a cancels and minus tan theta is left
chain rule through the parameter theta

steps.why: For a curve given by a parameter, dy/dx is the ratio of the two θ-derivatives. Writing dy/dθ alone and calling it the slope is the most common error at this line.
common_mistakes: Dividing dx/dθ by dy/dθ, which turns the slope upside down.
Losing the minus sign that comes from differentiating cos³θ.
Calling dy/dθ the slope of the tangent.
steps.memory_tip: Top over bottom, both with respect to θ: dy/dθ goes above, dx/dθ goes below.

steps.label: Write the tangent and read off A and B
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Reduce the tangent to intercept form x/A + y/B = 1. Once it is in that form the two intercepts are read straight off with no further working.
lines: Tangent at P:  y − a sin³θ = −tanθ (x − a cos³θ)
Multiply both sides by cosθ:
y cosθ − a sin³θ cosθ = −x sinθ + a sinθ cos³θ
x sinθ + y cosθ = a sinθ cos³θ + a sin³θ cosθ
= a sinθ cosθ (cos²θ + sin²θ) = a sinθ cosθ
Divide by a sinθ cosθ:   x/(a cosθ) + y/(a sinθ) = 1
This is the intercept form, so the tangent meets the axes at
A = (a cosθ, 0)   and   B = (0, a sinθ)

recall.must_convey: That the tangent reduces to x/(a cosθ) + y/(a sinθ) = 1, so A = (a cosθ, 0) and B = (0, a sinθ).
accept: write the tangent and put it in intercept form
x over a cos theta plus y over a sin theta equals one
the x intercept is a cos theta and the y intercept is a sin theta
intercept form lo pettite A and B direct ga vasthayi
put y equal to zero for A and x equal to zero for B
the right side simplifies to a sin theta cos theta

steps.why: The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 collapses the whole right side to a sinθ cosθ in one line, and dividing by it produces intercept form directly. Putting y = 0 and x = 0 into the unsimplified tangent gives the same two intercepts but takes twice the algebra.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply through by cosθ, so tanθ stays and the algebra does not close.
Reading the intercepts as a sinθ and a cosθ, with the two swapped.
Dividing by a sinθ cosθ but leaving the right side as something other than 1.
steps.memory_tip: Intercept form is x/A + y/B = 1, so whatever sits under x is the x-intercept and whatever sits under y is the y-intercept.

steps.label: Find AB and show it is free of θ
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The examiner is looking for θ to disappear. Stopping at √(a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ) does not answer the question, because the question asks for a constant.
lines: A = (a cosθ, 0),   B = (0, a sinθ)
AB = √((a cosθ − 0)² + (0 − a sinθ)²)
= √(a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ)
= √(a²(cos²θ + sin²θ)) = √(a²) = |a|

lines.text: ∴ AB = |a|, which contains no θ — the length AB is the same at every point of the curve, so it is a constant.

recall.must_convey: That AB = |a| because cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 removes θ, so the length is constant.
accept: use the distance formula and cos squared plus sin squared is one
A B comes to mod a which has no theta in it
the length is a so it is the same at every point
theta poyi kevalam a migulutundi so it is constant
distance between a cos theta zero and zero a sin theta is a
the answer does not depend on the point chosen

steps.why: A constant means free of the parameter. The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 is what removes θ, and saying so is the sentence that finishes the proof.
common_mistakes: Writing √(a²) as a and losing the modulus when a could be negative.
Leaving the answer as √(a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ) and calling it constant without simplifying.
Using the distance formula between P and A instead of between A and B.
steps.memory_tip: A sits on the x-axis and B sits on the y-axis, so AB is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs a cosθ and a sinθ — and that hypotenuse is |a|.

insider_note: Use the parametric point (a cos³θ, a sin³θ) — the implicit form makes the intercepts far messier. AB then comes out as |a|, free of θ, which is the whole claim.
